subscription_products.product_name: Hill's Science Diet Puppy Large Breed Chicken & Brown Rice Recipe Dry Dog Food, 27.5-lb bag
subscription_products.subscription_rationale: Daily staple. Large-breed puppy at 2 months and 30 lb needs a growth formula. Estimate: ~3 cups/day for a growing 30-lb large-breed puppy → 3 cups × 30 days = 90 cups/month. Typical kibble density ≈ 4 cups per lb → 27.5-lb bag ≈ 110 cups. 110 cups ÷ 90 cups/month ≈ 1.22 months per bag (≈5.5 weeks). Auto-ship avoids a last-minute run for food and keeps diet consistent (and it's beef-free formula choice).
subscription_products.personalized_note: Mario is a big-growing Golden at 2 months and 30 lb — this large-breed puppy formula will support steady growth and joint development while avoiding beef (important given his allergy). I recommend starting on a 27.5-lb bag on autoship so you never run out during busy house-training weeks.

subscription_products.product_name: American Kennel Club Extra Large Dog Training Pads, 28 x 30-in, Fresh Scented, 100 count
subscription_products.subscription_rationale: High-use consumable during apartment house-training. Estimate: Mario will likely need multiple pads/day while learning (conservative 3–5/day). Using 4 pads/day → 4 × 30 = 120 pads/month. 100-count pack covers ~25 days at 4/day → need ~1.2 packs/month. A monthly or 3–4 week autoship keeps pads on hand.
subscription_products.personalized_note: Since Mario is only 2 months and you don't have a yard, pads will be used heavily while you build a routine. Autoship for a 100‑count pack keeps you stocked so Mario always has a clean spot during training.

subscription_products.product_name: The Original Poop Bags Countdown USDA Certified Biobased Rolls, Unscented, 120 count
subscription_products.subscription_rationale: Daily outdoor pickup is a consumable. Estimate: 1–2 outdoor trips per day with one bag each → 1.5 bags/day average × 30 = 45 bags/month. 120-count roll ÷ 45 ≈ 2.6 months. A 2–3 month autoship cadence keeps a fresh supply without overstocking.
subscription_products.personalized_note: Mario lives in an apartment, so you'll be using bags every time you head out. This unscented 120‑count roll is convenient — you'll have plenty for month-to-month walks without worrying about spills or sticky hands.

Autoship every 1–2 weeks avoids running out during critical learning windows.
subscription_products.personalized_note: Mario is at prime training age — these peanut-butter, chicken-free soft treats are perfect for many quick rewards during sessions. They avoid beef (important for his allergy) and will keep him eager to learn.

subscription_products.product_name: Pupford Chicken Soft & Chewy Training Dog Treats, 10-oz pouch
subscription_products.subscription_rationale: Additional training-treat variety for daily reinforcement. Autoship every 2–3 weeks keeps a larger pouch on hand to alternate flavors and keep Mario motivated.
subscription_products.personalized_note: Rotating treats helps keep Mario excited during short apartment training sessions. This chicken-flavored pouch is beef-free and a great backup to the peanut-butter treats.

subscription_products.product_name: Zesty Paws All-in-One Bacon Flavored Soft & Chewy Training Bites Multivitamin Dog Treats, 12-oz bag

overall_strategy: Because Mario is a 2‑month‑old, 30‑lb Golden Retriever living in an apartment with no yard (and a beef allergy), Month 1–2 prioritizes setup essentials (crate, bed, harness, bowls, ID) and heavy short-term consumables that support intensive house‑training and early training (puppy food, training pads, soft treats, enzyme cleaners, poop bags, dental supplies). I selected consumables to subscribe to at cadences matching expected depletion from Mario's size and training frequency (food ~ every 6 weeks; pads and small training treat bags every 1–4 weeks; cleaners and toothpaste every 2–12 weeks), while marking durable, seasonal, and enrichment items as one‑time buys (cooling mat, crate, playpen, puzzle feeders, grooming tools). This mix keeps Mario fed, clean, and supported through critical early training without over-subscribing to long-lasting toys or gear, and it avoids beef‑based products given his allergy.
